"""How text written for later names a moment: always with its day.

Notifications, log lines and gap lists are read later than they are written,
so relative words ("dziś") would go stale and a bare "16:00" leaves the day
to guess. Every moment is spelled out the way the panel writes days that are
not today or tomorrow (``frontend/src/when.ts``): "pt 24.10 16:00", with the
year when it is not the current one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime

from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util

# datetime.weekday(): Monday is 0.
_WEEKDAY = ("pon", "wt", "śr", "czw", "pt", "sob", "nd")


def moment_label(moment: datetime) -> str:
    """``moment`` in local time with its day: "pt 24.10 16:00"."""
    local = dt_util.as_local(moment)
    year = f".{local.year}" if local.year != dt_util.now().year else ""
    return f"{_WEEKDAY[local.weekday()]} {local:%d.%m}{year} {local:%H:%M}"

# ADR 002: A durable record of missed plan actions

Status: accepted, 2026-10-24

## Context

PowerPilot has no actuator: Dawid or his automations carry out the plan. The
plan is recomputed every hour and on every relevant state flip, so an action it
asked for and nobody took disappears with the next plan. The car not plugged in
for a cheap hour, or the apartment left on the wrong meter, leaves no trace:

- The hour's vintage is recorded at the hour's first run, after the plan has
  already adapted to reality. The plug gates the running hour (an unplugged car
  gets no charging in it) and the running hour is planned on the apartment's
  actual supply, so the vintage of an hour that was missed reads as if nothing
  had been asked.
- The previous hour's vintage holds the plan from the start of that hour, not
  the last word before the boundary: mid-hour revisions record only the running
  hour's own row.
- The plan-vs-realization card compares an hour with its own vintage, and the
  ESS "plan not executed" watchdog is a live alarm kept in memory. Vintages are
  pruned after 30 days.

## Decision

**The ask.** After every plan run the coordinator keeps the plan's row for the
next clock hour: EV energy and minutes, the apartment's supply, the inverter
mode and the hour's price. That is what the panel's "Następna godzina" column
and the recommendation entities show. It is persisted with the snapshots; when
the hour begins, its last ask is frozen as that hour's ask, persisted, and
written into that hour's vintage as `ask`.

**A miss** is reality contradicting the running hour's ask on something a person
or an automation controls. At most one record per hour and kind:

| Kind | Found when |
|---|---|
| `ev_unplugged` | the ask charges the car (> 0.05 kWh), the calendar has the car available that hour, the car is at home (tracker and presence) and the plug sensor reads unplugged at a run of that hour |
| `supply` | switching is modelled and the confirmed supply is not the meter the ask placed the apartment on, at a run of that hour |
| `ess` | the watchdog's alarm: one record per episode, from the alarm going on to it going off |
| `ev_off_plan` | EV energy in an hour none of its plans asked for (the series' existing rule, now one shared function), recorded when the hour settles |

Without a plug sensor, or with the car's whereabouts unknown, no `ev_unplugged`
miss is recorded: nothing says the cable could have gone in.

**What it cost.** When an `ev_unplugged` or `supply` miss is found, the refresh's
inputs are solved once more with the ask honoured for the rest of the running
hour: the car on the cable, or the apartment on the asked meter as if switched
at the hour's start. The miss costs the plan's PLN objective of reality minus
that of this counterfactual. It is the re-solve the switch recommendations
already value cycles with, so it accounts for the monthly price cap, the battery
and wherever the plan moved the energy. The objective is taken without the cycle
thresholds, the reserve-recovery penalty and the `#ess` bonus
(`Plan.objective_pln`), which are not money.

When the hour ends, the cost is scaled by the share of the miss that stayed
missed: the EV energy the counterfactual would have charged in the rest of the
hour against what the car took after the miss was found (5-minute statistics),
or the minutes on the wrong meter until the supply log confirmed the switch.
The confirmation lags the flip by the detector's samples, so a late switch
counts a few minutes long. A counterfactual that charges nothing in the rest
of the hour keeps its full cost. A negative cost is kept: by then, following the
plan would have cost more. `ess` and `ev_off_plan` carry no cost, with a note:
the model cannot say what the inverter did instead, and charging nothing asked
for has no planned hour to compare against.

**Storage.** An append-only ledger in its own store,
`powerpilot_<entry>_misses`. It is never pruned and never cleared, not by
"Wyczyść dane" either: it is a record of what happened, not a cache. A record is
open until its hour settles (an ESS episode until the alarm ends), then frozen.
An unreadable file is moved aside (`.corrupt-<date>`), the panel says so, and a
new ledger starts next to it.

**Restarts.** The asks are persisted, a found miss is saved at once, and
settlement reads the recorder and the supply log, so a restart loses nothing
but the watchdog's live state. An ESS episode still open at startup is closed at
its last confirmation, with a note that a restart ended it.

**History.** Hours before this version have no ask, so they have no
`ev_unplugged` or `supply` records. `ev_off_plan` is backfilled from the
vintages that still exist (30 days).

**Shown.** A "Niewykonane zalecenia planu" card on "Przegląd", below the control
card: counts and costs for 7 and 30 days, then the records, newest first, with
the moment and its day, what the plan asked for, what happened and the cost. The
control card's hour columns flag their hour's misses. Each found miss is logged.
`powerpilot/misses` serves the records.

## Rejected

- **The ask taken from the previous hour's vintage (index 1).** It is the plan
  from the start of the previous hour and misses that hour's revisions, so it
  would invent asks the plan had already withdrawn.
- **Displaced energy times a price difference** (the kWh the car missed times
  the price where the plan moved them minus the price asked for). It ignores the
  monthly cap, under which moving energy between hours can cost nothing, and the
  battery, which the EV shares a phase with. The re-solve prices both.
- **Valuing a miss at settlement from recorded prices.** The counterfactual
  needs the model's inputs at the moment of the miss, which are gone by then.
- **Keeping the records in the vintages.** They are pruned after 30 days.
- **A notification per miss.** Notifications are for acting now; a miss is
  history by the time it is recorded.

"""``Plan.objective_pln``: the horizon's spend in złoty, whatever steers the solver.

A missed plan action is costed by solving the same inputs twice — reality and
the plan followed — and subtracting (ADR 002). That only means PLN if the
number compared is money: the solver's own objective prices only what it can
move (the house's demand and the EV's planned load are constants it never
sees) and carries steering terms worth far more than any price (the
reserve-recovery penalty, the ``#ess`` bonus).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import timedelta

import pytest
from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util

from custom_components.powerpilot.battery import BatteryModel
from custom_components.powerpilot.models import ESSRequest, Forecast, HourSlot
from custom_components.powerpilot.optimizer import ChargeCurve, Optimizer, OptimizerConfig

WEAR = 0.05
ETA = 0.95


def _start():
    # Whole future hours only: the running hour is scaled to its remaining minutes.
    return dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(hours=1)


def _forecast(prices: list[float], demand: float = 0.6) -> Forecast:
    start = _start()
    return Forecast(
        slots=[
            HourSlot(
                start=start + timedelta(hours=i),
                buy_price=price,
                distribution_price_kwh=0.1,
                base_consumption_kwh=demand,
            )
            for i, price in enumerate(prices)
        ]
    )


def _battery(soc: float, recovering: bool = False) -> BatteryModel:
    return BatteryModel(
        capacity_kwh=10.0,
        charge_efficiency=ETA,
        discharge_efficiency=ETA,
        wear_cost=WEAR,
        min_soc=10.0,
        max_soc=100.0,
        soc=soc,
        energy_cost=0.5,
        recovering=recovering,
    )


def _optimizer() -> Optimizer:
    return Optimizer(
        OptimizerConfig(
            inverter_max_charge_kw=1.0,
            inverter_max_discharge_kw=3.0,
            charge_curve=ChargeCurve(default_kw=1.0),
            # No value for energy left at the end: the spend is then the grid
            # bill plus wear, which the test can add up from the decisions.
            terminal_price=0.0,
        )
    )


def _spend(plan) -> float:
    """The plan's bill from its own decisions: grid at the hour's price, plus wear."""
    total = 0.0
    for decision, slot in zip(plan.decisions, plan.forecast.slots):
        total += decision.grid_buy_kwh * slot.total_price_kwh
        total += WEAR * (ETA * decision.battery_charge_kwh + decision.battery_discharge_kwh)
    return total


def test_the_objective_in_pln_is_the_bill() -> None:
    plan = _optimizer().optimize(_forecast([0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.1]), _battery(soc=40.0))
    assert plan.objective_pln == pytest.approx(_spend(plan), abs=1e-3)
    # The solver's objective leaves the house's own demand out entirely.
    assert plan.comparable_cost_pln < plan.objective_pln - 1.0


def test_the_recovery_penalty_is_not_money() -> None:
    # 1 kW from 2 % of 10 kWh: the reserve target (min + margin) is hours
    # away, so the penalty is paid in every one of them.
    plan = _optimizer().optimize(_forecast([0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4]), _battery(soc=2.0))
    assert plan.comparable_cost_pln > 1000.0
    assert plan.objective_pln == pytest.approx(_spend(plan), abs=1e-3)


def test_the_ess_bonus_is_not_money() -> None:
    forecast = _forecast([0.9, 0.9, 0.9])
    forced = {forecast.slots[1].start}
    plan = _optimizer().optimize(
        forecast, _battery(soc=40.0), ess_request=ESSRequest(forced_hours=forced)
    )
    assert plan.decisions[1].battery_charge_kwh > 0.5
    assert plan.comparable_cost_pln < -500.0
    assert plan.objective_pln == pytest.approx(_spend(plan), abs=1e-3)

"""The rules of missed plan actions (``misses.py``, ADR 002).

The plan is recomputed all the time, so an action it asked for and nobody took
vanishes with the next plan. These pin what counts as a miss, what it cost, and
that the record of it is never lost or rewritten.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from custom_components.powerpilot.misses import (
    KIND_ESS,
    KIND_EV_UNPLUGGED,
    NOTE_NO_EV_STATS,
    NOTE_NOT_COSTED,
    Ask,
    Counterfactual,
    MissLedger,
    PlanAsks,
    Settlement,
    ask_from_plan,
    counterfactual,
    ess_record,
    ev_left_unplugged,
    ev_off_plan,
    ev_unplugged_record,
    followed_transition_at,
    miss_id,
    settle_ev_unplugged,
    settle_supply,
    supply_not_followed,
    supply_record,
    switch_moment,
)
from custom_components.powerpilot.models import Decision, Forecast, HourSlot, Plan

H = datetime(2026, 10, 24, 13, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def _ask(hour: datetime = H, **fields) -> Ask:
    values = {
        "at": hour - timedelta(minutes=20),
        "ev_kwh": 5.5,
        "ev_minutes": 60,
        "supply": None,
        "mode": "passthrough",
        "charge_power_kw": 0.0,
        "price_kwh": 0.45,
        **fields,
    }
    return Ask(hour=hour, **values)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the ask


def test_the_hour_begins_with_the_last_ask_made_for_it() -> None:
    asks = PlanAsks()
    asks.offer(_ask(ev_kwh=1.0))
    asks.offer(_ask(ev_kwh=5.5))  # a later plan before the boundary
    assert asks.begin(H).ev_kwh == 5.5
    # A re-plan inside the hour offers the NEXT hour; this hour's ask stays.
    asks.offer(_ask(H + timedelta(hours=1), ev_kwh=0.0))
    assert asks.begin(H).ev_kwh == 5.5
    assert asks.begin(H + timedelta(hours=1)).ev_kwh == 0.0


def test_an_ask_for_another_hour_is_no_ask() -> None:
    """Home Assistant down across the boundary: the offer was for an hour that
    has passed, and an older plan's view is not borrowed."""
    asks = PlanAsks(upcoming=_ask(H - timedelta(hours=1)))
    assert asks.begin(H) is None


def test_asks_survive_a_restart() -> None:
    asks = PlanAsks(current=_ask(), upcoming=_ask(H + timedelta(hours=1), supply="meter_2"))
    restored = PlanAsks.from_dict(asks.to_dict())
    assert restored.current == asks.current
    assert restored.upcoming == asks.upcoming


def test_an_unreadable_ask_is_an_error_not_a_silent_gap() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        PlanAsks.from_dict({"current": {"hour": "noon"}})


def _plan(*, supply_switching: bool) -> Plan:
    slots = [
        HourSlot(start=H + timedelta(hours=i), buy_price=0.3, distribution_price_kwh=0.15)
        for i in range(2)
    ]
    decisions = [
        Decision(start=slots[0].start, inverter_mode="passthrough", supply="victron"),
        Decision(
            start=slots[1].start,
            inverter_mode="charge",
            charge_power_kw=3.0,
            ev_charge=True,
            ev_charge_kwh=5.5,
            ev_charge_minutes=60,
            supply="meter_2",
        ),
    ]
    return Plan(
        forecast=Forecast(slots=slots), decisions=decisions, supply_switching=supply_switching
    )


def test_the_ask_is_the_plans_row_for_that_hour() -> None:
    ask = ask_from_plan(_plan(supply_switching=True), H + timedelta(hours=1), H)
    assert (ask.ev_kwh, ask.ev_minutes, ask.supply, ask.mode) == (5.5, 60, "meter_2", "charge")
    assert ask.price_kwh == pytest.approx(0.45)
    assert ask_from_plan(_plan(supply_switching=True), H + timedelta(hours=5), H) is None


def test_a_plan_not_free_to_switch_asks_nothing_of_the_apartment() -> None:
    ask = ask_from_plan(_plan(supply_switching=False), H + timedelta(hours=1), H)
    assert ask.supply is None


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ a miss


def test_the_car_left_unplugged_at_home_is_a_miss() -> None:
    assert ev_left_unplugged(_ask(), plugged=False, home=True, calendar_available=True)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ask", "plugged", "home", "available"),
    [
        (_ask(ev_kwh=0.04), False, True, True),  # nothing asked
        (_ask(), True, True, True),  # on the cable
        (_ask(), None, True, True),  # plug unknown
        (_ask(), False, None, True),  # whereabouts unknown
        (_ask(), False, False, True),  # away: nobody could plug it in
        (_ask(), False, True, False),  # the calendar has it away
    ],
)
def test_no_miss_unless_every_reading_says_the_cable_could_have_gone_in(
    ask, plugged, home, available
) -> None:
    assert not ev_left_unplugged(ask, plugged=plugged, home=home, calendar_available=available)


def test_the_apartment_on_the_other_meter_is_a_miss() -> None:
    assert supply_not_followed(_ask(supply="meter_2"), "victron")
    assert not supply_not_followed(_ask(supply="meter_2"), "meter_2")
    assert not supply_not_followed(_ask(supply=None), "victron")  # nothing asked
    assert not supply_not_followed(_ask(supply="meter_2"), None)  # actual unknown


def _transition(state: str, at: datetime):
    return SimpleNamespace(state=state, at=at)


def test_not_switched_when_asked_counts_as_switched_at_the_hours_start() -> None:
    log = [_transition("victron", H - timedelta(days=3))]
    assert followed_transition_at(log, "meter_2", H) == H


def test_switched_away_against_the_ask_counts_as_never_switched() -> None:
    before = H - timedelta(days=3)
    log = [_transition("victron", before), _transition("meter_2", H + timedelta(minutes=20))]
    assert followed_transition_at(log, "victron", H) == before


def test_the_switch_moment_is_the_first_logged_switch_to_the_asked_meter() -> None:
    found = H + timedelta(minutes=1)
    log = [
        _transition("meter_2", H - timedelta(days=1)),
        _transition("victron", H + timedelta(minutes=12)),
        _transition("meter_2", H + timedelta(minutes=40)),
    ]
    assert switch_moment(log, "victron", found, H + timedelta(hours=1)) == H + timedelta(
        minutes=12
    )
    assert switch_moment(log, "victron", H + timedelta(minutes=13), H + timedelta(hours=1)) is None


def _off_plan(**overrides) -> bool:
    values = {
        "realized_kwh": 3.0,
        "planned_kwh": 0.0,
        "planned_before_kwh": 0.0,
        "watched": True,
        "away": False,
        "spill_kwh": 1.8,
    }
    return ev_off_plan(**{**values, **overrides})


def test_charging_no_plan_asked_for_is_off_plan() -> None:
    assert _off_plan()


def test_off_plan_needs_a_plan_to_contradict() -> None:
    assert not _off_plan(planned_kwh=None)  # no vintage
    assert not _off_plan(watched=False)  # older than revision tracking
    assert not _off_plan(planned_kwh=2.0)  # a plan of the hour asked for it
    assert not _off_plan(away=True)  # charged on a trip
    assert not _off_plan(realized_kwh=None)  # not measured


def test_a_session_overrunning_a_planned_hour_is_not_off_plan() -> None:
    assert not _off_plan(realized_kwh=1.5, planned_before_kwh=5.0)
    assert _off_plan(realized_kwh=1.9, planned_before_kwh=5.0)
    assert _off_plan(realized_kwh=1.5, planned_before_kwh=0.0)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the cost


def _record_with_cf(record: dict, delta: float | None, ev_kwh: float | None = None, error=None):
    record["cf"] = Counterfactual(delta, ev_kwh, error).to_dict()
    return record


def test_the_cost_is_reality_minus_the_plan_followed() -> None:
    reality = SimpleNamespace(objective_pln=12.40)
    followed = SimpleNamespace(
        objective_pln=11.85,
        decision_at=lambda hour: SimpleNamespace(ev_charge_kwh=5.2),
    )
    cf = counterfactual(reality, followed, H)
    assert cf.delta_pln == pytest.approx(0.55)
    assert cf.ev_kwh == 5.2


def test_a_car_never_plugged_in_costs_the_whole_difference() -> None:
    record = _record_with_cf(ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H), 0.55, ev_kwh=5.5)
    settled = settle_ev_unplugged(record, delivered_after_kwh=0.0, delivered_hour_kwh=0.0)
    assert settled.cost_pln == 0.55

def test_plugging_in_later_in_the_hour_scales_the_cost() -> None:

def test_a_counterfactual_that_charges_nothing_keeps_its_cost() -> None:
    record = _record_with_cf(ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H), 0.12, ev_kwh=0.0)

def test_a_negative_cost_is_kept() -> None:

def test_a_late_switch_costs_the_minutes_on_the_wrong_meter() -> None:

    assert settle_supply(record, H + timedelta(minutes=15)).cost_pln == 0.25
    assert settle_supply(record, None).cost_pln == 1.00

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the ledger


def test_a_record_is_added_once_and_never_overwritten() -> None:
    ledger = MissLedger()
    first = ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H)
    assert ledger.add(first)
    assert not ledger.add(ev_unplugged_record(_ask(ev_kwh=9.0), H + timedelta(minutes=30)))
    assert ledger.get(miss_id(KIND_EV_UNPLUGGED, H))["asked"]["ev_kwh"] == 5.5


def test_a_record_is_settled_once() -> None:
    ledger = MissLedger()
    record = ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H)
    ledger.add(record)
    assert ledger.set_counterfactual(record["id"], Counterfactual(0.5, 5.5))
    assert not ledger.set_counterfactual(record["id"], Counterfactual(9.9, 5.5))
    later = H + timedelta(hours=2)
    assert ledger.settle(record["id"], Settlement(0.5, None, {"ev_kwh": 0.0}), later)
    assert not ledger.settle(record["id"], Settlement(7.0, "x", {}), later)
    assert not ledger.touch(record["id"], ev_kwh=3.0)
    assert ledger.get(record["id"])["cost_pln"] == 0.5
    assert ledger.open_records() == []


def test_the_ledger_survives_a_restart_whole() -> None:
    ledger = MissLedger(off_plan_through=H)
    ledger.add(ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H))
    ledger.add(ess_record(H + timedelta(minutes=7), "charge", 3.0, "ESS oddał 0.30 kWh"))
    restored = MissLedger.from_dict(ledger.to_dict())
    assert restored.records() == ledger.records()
    assert restored.off_plan_through == H
    assert restored.get(miss_id(KIND_ESS, H + timedelta(minutes=7)))["kind"] == KIND_ESS


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "stored",
    [
        "not a ledger",
        {"records": {}},
        {"records": [{"id": "x"}]},
        {"records": [{**ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H), "kind": "mystery"}]},
        {"records": [{**ev_unplugged_record(_ask(), H), "hour": "noon"}]},
    ],
)
def test_an_unreadable_ledger_is_refused_whole(stored) -> None:
    """A record dropped quietly on load would be gone at the next save."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        MissLedger.from_dict(stored)

def _vintage(hour, ev: list[float]) -> dict:
    """Minimal vintage for ``hour`` planning ``ev`` kWh over its horizon."""
    return {
        "run_at": hour.isoformat(),
        "start": hour.isoformat(),
        "n": len(ev),

def _with_ev_meter(coordinator, readings: dict) -> None:

async def test_series_flags_ev_charging_no_plan_asked_for(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
) -> None:
    """Realized EV energy in an hour no plan ever scheduled raises the flag."""
    coordinator = await _setup(hass)
    hour = dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
    past_hour = hour - timedelta(hours=1)

    # A vintage backs the past hour, and it planned no EV charging.
    coordinator.snapshots.add(_vintage(past_hour, [0.0, 0.0]))
    _with_ev_meter(coordinator, {past_hour: 7.5})

    result = await coordinator.get_series(past_hours=2)
    row = next(h for h in result["hours"] if h["start"] == past_hour.isoformat())
    assert row["ev_off_plan"] is True

    # Once a mid-hour revision shows the charging WAS planned, the flag clears —
    # that is the whole difference between a decision and a surprise.
    coordinator.snapshots.add_revision(past_hour, {"at": "x", "why": "kabel", "ev": 7.5})
    result = await coordinator.get_series(past_hours=2)
    row = next(h for h in result["hours"] if h["start"] == past_hour.isoformat())
    assert row["ev_off_plan"] is None
    assert row["revisions"][0]["why"] == "kabel"

    hour = dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
    spill_hour = hour - timedelta(hours=1)

    # Under 10 minutes at the configured 3.5 kW → the session finishing.

    _with_ev_meter(coordinator, {spill_hour: 5.0})
    result = await coordinator.get_series(past_hours=3)
    row = next(h for h in result["hours"] if h["start"] == spill_hour.isoformat())
    assert row["ev_off_plan"] is True

"""Missed plan actions recorded by the coordinator (ADR 002).

The pure rules are in ``test_misses.py``; these pin the wiring: what the plan
asked of an hour is kept across the boundary and a restart, a miss is found
from the live states and costed by solving the ask followed, it is settled
from the recorder and the supply log once its hour is over, the watchdog's
alarm becomes episodes, and none of it is ever deleted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import timedelta
from types import SimpleNamespace

from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
from pytest_homeassistant_custom_component.common import MockConfigEntry

from custom_components.powerpilot import coordinator as coordinator_module
from custom_components.powerpilot.const import (
    CONF_EV_ENABLED,
    CONF_EV_ENERGY_ADDED_SENSOR,
    CONF_EV_LOCATION_SENSOR,
    CONF_EV_PLUG_SENSOR,
    CONF_SOC_SENSOR,
    DEFAULTS,
    DOMAIN,
)
from custom_components.powerpilot.misses import (
    KIND_ESS,
    KIND_EV_OFF_PLAN,
    KIND_EV_UNPLUGGED,
    KIND_SUPPLY,
    Ask,
    Counterfactual,
    miss_id,
    supply_record,
)
from custom_components.powerpilot.models import SupplyPlanning
from custom_components.powerpilot.modules.snapshots import SnapshotStore

ENTRY_ID = "misses_entry"
EV = {
    CONF_EV_ENABLED: True,
    CONF_EV_PLUG_SENSOR: "binary_sensor.plug",
    CONF_EV_LOCATION_SENSOR: "device_tracker.car",
}


async def _setup(hass: HomeAssistant, **config):
    hass.states.async_set("sensor.soc", "55", {"unit_of_measurement": "%"})
    entry = MockConfigEntry(
        domain=DOMAIN,
        entry_id=ENTRY_ID,
        data={**DEFAULTS, CONF_SOC_SENSOR: "sensor.soc", **config},
        title="PowerPilot",
    )
    entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    assert await hass.config_entries.async_setup(entry.entry_id)
    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)
    coordinator = hass.data[DOMAIN][entry.entry_id]

    async def _empty_recent_soc(*args):
        return {}

    coordinator._recent_soc = _empty_recent_soc
    return coordinator


def _hour():
    return dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)


def _ask(hour, **fields) -> Ask:
    values = {
        "at": hour - timedelta(minutes=10),
        "ev_kwh": 5.5,
        "ev_minutes": 60,
        "supply": None,
        "mode": "passthrough",
        "charge_power_kw": 0.0,
        "price_kwh": 0.45,
        **fields,
    }
    return Ask(hour=hour, **values)


async def _refresh(hass, coordinator) -> None:
    await coordinator.async_refresh()
    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the ask


async def test_the_next_hours_ask_is_kept_with_the_snapshots(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
    coordinator = await _setup(hass)
    upcoming = coordinator.plan_asks.upcoming
    assert upcoming is not None
    assert upcoming.hour == _hour() + timedelta(hours=1)
    decision = coordinator.data.decision_at(upcoming.hour)
    assert upcoming.mode == decision.inverter_mode
    assert coordinator._snapshots_payload()["asks"]["upcoming"]["hour"] == upcoming.hour.isoformat()


async def test_an_hour_begins_with_its_ask_written_into_its_vintage(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
) -> None:
    """The vintage is the plan already adapted to reality; the ask is what was
    asked before it, kept beside it."""
    coordinator = await _setup(hass)
    hour = _hour()
    coordinator.snapshots = SnapshotStore()
    coordinator._last_snapshot_hour = None
    coordinator.plan_asks.current = None
    coordinator.plan_asks.upcoming = _ask(hour, ev_kwh=4.2)

    await _refresh(hass, coordinator)

    assert coordinator.plan_asks.current.ev_kwh == 4.2
    vintage = coordinator.snapshots.get(dt_util.as_utc(hour).isoformat())
    assert vintage["ask"]["ev_kwh"] == 4.2


async def test_asks_are_restored_after_a_restart(hass: HomeAssistant, hass_storage) -> None:
    hour = _hour()
    asks = {"current": None, "upcoming": _ask(hour, ev_kwh=3.3).to_dict()}
    hass_storage[f"{DOMAIN}_{ENTRY_ID}_snapshots"] = {
        "version": 1,
        "key": f"{DOMAIN}_{ENTRY_ID}_snapshots",
        "data": {"records": {}, "asks": asks},
    }
    coordinator = await _setup(hass)
    # The first run after the restart began the hour with the stored ask.
    assert coordinator.plan_asks.current.ev_kwh == 3.3


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ finding


async def test_a_car_left_unplugged_at_home_is_recorded_and_costed(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
) -> None:
    hass.states.async_set("binary_sensor.plug", "off")
    hass.states.async_set("device_tracker.car", "home")
    coordinator = await _setup(hass, **EV)
    hour = _hour()
    coordinator.plan_asks.current = _ask(hour)

    await _refresh(hass, coordinator)

    record = coordinator.misses.get(miss_id(KIND_EV_UNPLUGGED, hour))
    assert record is not None
    assert record["asked"]["ev_kwh"] == 5.5
    assert record["actual"] == {"plugged": False, "home": True}
    # Its counterfactual was solved after the plan was out.
    assert record["cf"] is not None and record["cf"]["error"] is None
    assert isinstance(record["cf"]["delta_pln"], float)
    assert any("niepodłączone" in (e.get("message") or "") for e in coordinator.get_log())

    # Found once: another run in the same hour adds nothing.
    await _refresh(hass, coordinator)
    assert len(coordinator.misses) == 1


async def test_no_miss_while_the_car_is_away(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
    hass.states.async_set("binary_sensor.plug", "off")
    hass.states.async_set("device_tracker.car", "not_home")
    coordinator = await _setup(hass, **EV)
    coordinator.plan_asks.current = _ask(_hour())

    await _refresh(hass, coordinator)

    assert len(coordinator.misses) == 0


async def test_the_apartment_on_the_other_meter_is_costed_as_if_switched(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
) -> None:
    coordinator = await _setup(hass)
    hour = _hour()
    now = hour + timedelta(minutes=3)
    ask = _ask(hour, supply="meter_2", ev_kwh=0.0)
    planning = SupplyPlanning(actual="victron")
    solved: list = []

    def solve(supply=None):
        solved.append(supply)
        return coordinator.data

    pending = coordinator._find_misses(ask, now, None, solve, None, planning)

    record = coordinator.misses.get(miss_id(KIND_SUPPLY, hour))
    assert record["actual"] == {"supply": "victron"}
    (record_id, followed), = pending
    assert record_id == record["id"]
    followed()
    assert solved[0].actual == "meter_2"
    assert solved[0].last_transition_at == hour  # as if switched as the hour began


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ settling


async def test_a_late_switch_is_settled_by_its_minutes_on_the_wrong_meter(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
) -> None:

async def async_setup_entry(hass: HomeAssistant, entry: ConfigEntry) -> bool:
    """Set up PowerPilot from a config entry."""
    _migrate_calendar_option(hass, entry)
    _migrate_climate_option(hass, entry)
    # Day-of-week tariff periods classify future days (weekends/holidays) via
    # ``workday.check_date``. That service is a hard requirement — we never
    # second-guess it. If it isn't registered yet (workday still loading, or the
    # integration removed/broken), defer setup and let HA retry; PowerPilot does
    # not start until the service is available.
    if _uses_day_sensor(entry) and not hass.services.has_service(
        _WORKDAY_DOMAIN, _CHECK_DATE_SERVICE
    ):
        raise ConfigEntryNotReady(
            f"Serwis {_WORKDAY_DOMAIN}.{_CHECK_DATE_SERVICE} niedostępny — "
            "integracja workday nie jest gotowa, a taryfy używają czujnika dnia. "
            "Ponowię konfigurację, gdy serwis się pojawi."
        )

    # Don't start until configured entities exist and report a usable value.
    # Like other integrations, defer setup and let HA retry — this keeps the
    # entry in a clean "waiting for entities" state instead of coming up with a
    # half-broken plan when source integrations are still loading.
    unready = _unready_inputs(hass, entry)
    if unready:
        raise ConfigEntryNotReady(
            "Czujniki wejściowe niedostępne: "
            + ", ".join(unready)
            + ". Ponowię konfigurację, gdy będą gotowe."
        )

    coordinator = PowerPilotCoordinator(hass, entry)
    await coordinator.async_setup_modules()
    await coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh()

    hass.data.setdefault(DOMAIN, {})[entry.entry_id] = coordinator

(SoC/flows + prices incl. the battery-cost line). It needs the `apexcharts-card`

### Sidebar panel

PowerPilot also ships a **custom sidebar panel** (Lit + TypeScript, ApexCharts)
that registers itself automatically — a **PowerPilot** entry appears in the HA
sidebar with ten tabs: *Przegląd* (energy and price charts, the current control,
the apartment-supply card), *Ceny* (the hourly price archive), *Symulacje*
(forecast accuracy against what happened), *Przepływ* (a diagram of the installation — what is behind what, every sensor's reading and the arithmetic of each computed value — then the live pipeline),
*Sprawność* (measured vs configured efficiencies), *Status* (what works and
what is missing), *Diagnostyka*, *Profile* (learned consumption profiles),
*Logi* and *Debug* (a full state export). It is backed by a WebSocket API
(`powerpilot/plan`, `status`, `log`, `profiles`, `series`, `prices`,
`accuracy`, `flow`, `efficiency`, `debug`, `diagnostics`,
`consumption_stats`), not by entity attributes. See
[docs/INSTALL_AND_VERIFY.md](docs/INSTALL_AND_VERIFY.md) for how to verify and
[the frontend build notes](docs/INSTALL_AND_VERIFY.md#budowanie-frontendu-dla-deweloperów).

## Architecture

## Directory layout

```
custom_components/powerpilot/
  __init__.py          integration setup / unload
  manifest.json
  const.py             keys, defaults, enums-as-strings
  models.py            HourSlot, Forecast, Decision, Plan
  battery.py           BatteryModel (cost-after-losses)
  optimizer.py         heuristic optimizer
  forecast.py          ForecastBuilder
  coordinator.py       DataUpdateCoordinator running the pipeline
  config_flow.py       config + options flow
  sensor.py            output + plan sensors
  binary_sensor.py     ev_charge / ev_connect_charger
  modules/
    base.py            PowerPilotModule + registry
    prices.py          dynamic-tariff price sources (confirmed > forecast)
    tariff.py          distribution-tariff module (energy + distribution split)
    consumption.py     weekly consumption profile from a power sensor
    loads.py           scheduled extra loads (washer, dishwasher, ironing)
    ev.py              EV SoC / location / range → charging need
    weather.py         hourly temperature forecast
    climate.py         heating/cooling energy vs outside temperature
    calendar.py        Apple Calendar → trips → EV charging plan
  strings.json
  translations/{en,pl}.json
```

def test_the_ask_finds_the_repeated_hour_when_the_clocks_go_back() -> None:
    """25.10.2026 has two 02:00s in Warsaw; the plan's next hour after the first
    is the second, which wall-clock arithmetic would skip."""
    from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

    warsaw = ZoneInfo("Europe/Warsaw")
    first = datetime(2026, 10, 25, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)  # 02:00 CEST
    second = first + timedelta(hours=1)  # 02:00 CET
    slots = [

        for i in range(3)
    ]
    plan = Plan(
        forecast=Forecast(slots=slots),
        decisions=[Decision(start=slot.start, inverter_mode="passthrough") for slot in slots],
    )
    ask = ask_from_plan(plan, second, first)
    assert ask is not None and ask.hour == second
    assert ask.hour.astimezone(warsaw).hour == 2

git add custom_components/powerpilot/misses.py custom_components/powerpilot/const.py custom_components/powerpilot/coordinator.py custom_components/powerpilot/modules/ev.py custom_components/powerpilot/modules/snapshots.py custom_components/powerpilot/websocket_api.py docs/adr/002-missed-plan-actions.md docs/ARCHITECTURE.md tests/test_misses.py tests/test_missed_plan_actions.py tests/test_supply_notifications.py && git diff --cached --stat && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(misses): keep a record of plan actions nobody carried out

PowerPilot has no actuator and the plan is recomputed all the time, so an
action it asked for and nobody took vanished with the next plan: the plug
gates the running hour and the running hour is planned on the actual
supply, so even the hour's vintage read as if nothing had been asked.

After every run the coordinator now keeps the plan's row for the next hour
(the ask), persisted with the snapshots; when the hour begins the ask is
frozen and stored in its vintage. A run that sees reality contradict the
running hour's ask records a miss in an append-only ledger with its own
store (powerpilot_<entry>_misses), never pruned and kept by "Wyczyść dane":

- ev_unplugged: the ask charges the car, the calendar has it available,
  the tracker has it at home and the plug sensor reads unplugged;
- supply: the apartment is on the other meter than the ask;
- ess: the watchdog's alarm, one record per episode (a restart ends an open
  episode at its last confirmation);
- ev_off_plan: charging in an hour none of its plans asked for, recorded as
  the hour settles (backfilled from the vintages that are left); the rule
  is now one function shared with the chart series.

The first two are costed by solving the refresh's inputs again with the ask
followed (the car on the cable, the apartment on the asked meter) and
comparing Plan.objective_pln, so the cap, the battery and wherever the plan
moved the energy are priced. The counterfactual runs after the plan is
published. When the hour is over the cost is scaled by the energy (5-minute
statistics) or the minutes (the supply log) that stayed missed.
powerpilot/misses serves the ledger; series hours carry their misses.

Rejected (ADR 002): the ask read from the previous hour's vintage, which
misses its revisions; a price difference of the displaced energy, blind to
the monthly cap; keeping the records in the vintages, pruned after 30 days.

Hours are compared in UTC, so the repeated 02:00 when the clocks go back
gets its own ask.

Co-Authored-By: AI
EOF
